Job Title: SVP Personal Assistant

Department:  Global Regulatory & R&D Quality (GRQ)

Location: Soeborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As SVP Personal Assistant, you will keep the leadership of Global Regulatory & R&D Quality (GRQ) prepared, aligned and moving. You will run the rhythm of the SVP’s work, from meetings and offsites to annual processes and budget coordination, and lead the assistant community that supports the area. Your judgement and discretion free up time for the decisions that matter, so GRQ colleagues can move work forward with clarity and pace.

What you’ll bring

• A BA in business languages or equivalent, with a focus on English.

• 6-7 years of management administrative experience, including experience as a team coordinator and as a member of a management team.

• Fluent written and spoken English, and experience from an international business environment.

• Project management skills and experience working in a project-oriented, international matrix organisation.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Word and a good command of the Microsoft Office package, with experience of digital and AI productivity tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot.

• Knowledge of quality management systems, clinical development and basic medical terminology.

• Sound judgement, a high degree of discretion and strong ethical awareness when handling confidential information.

• A proactive, pragmatic and flexible approach, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to navigate many stakeholders in a diverse, multicultural setting.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience of supporting re-organisations, onboarding of senior managers or large-scale events.

What you’ll do

You will be the SVP’s trusted partner and gatekeeper, and the person who connects the GRQ leadership team, the wider area and the assistants who support them.

• Prepare the SVP for what matters: manage the calendar, travel and pre-reads, and act on the SVP’s behalf with discretion.

• Plan and drive meetings, offsites and events for the SVP and the management team, and help plan and carry out re-organisations.

• Lead cross-functional projects and processes in the SVP area, and coordinate onboarding for new senior managers.

• Coordinate annual People & Organisation processes with your P&O partner, and manage the GRQ Line of Business budget with your finance partner.

• Lead the assistant community in GRQ: set the meeting structure, share best practice, mentor colleagues, take part in recruiting new assistants and keep improving how the team works, including through AI and digital tools.

• Make sure legal documents, such as Powers of Attorney, are signed on time, and keep the SVP area website up to date.

Who you’ll work with

You will report to the SVP of GRQ and work every day with the SVP’s Executive Assistant. Without a formal reporting line, you will lead and coordinate the GRQ leadership team PA group of four PAs and the five Area Coordinators, and you will also take part in the R&D leadership team PA group.

Your wider network includes the GRQ leadership team and all RQ&C leaders, and your communication, P&O and finance partners. Outside Novo, you will work with external experts, boards, consultancies, agencies and vendors. The role spans cultures and colleagues from different parts of the world, and the way of working is not always spelled out. We trust you to bring structure, ask the clear question and speak up when things stall.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted with real room to manoeuvre and decide, supported by a close and trusting relationship with the SVP and the SVP’s Executive Assistant. You will grow your leadership skills by guiding a team of assistants without formal authority, and build new skills through project work, the R&D onboarding project for new assistants and the use of AI and digital tools in everyday work. You will help shape the Wellbeing committee across the SVP area, so colleagues can thrive as well as perform.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00  DKK , corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep a regulatory, quality and clinical reporting leadership team moving with clarity, apply for the SVP Personal Assistant role by 13th November 2026

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Strategy Director, Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS) IT, you will help shape strategic priorities and strengthen decision-making across a complex global organisation. Working closely with senior leaders, you will connect business and technology, create alignment across organisational boundaries and turn strategic ambition into clear direction and action.

What you'll bring

We are looking for a strategic partner who fosters trust, align stakeholders, and creates clarity in ambiguous situations. To succeed, you will bring:

• 
Solid experience supporting senior leaders and leadership teams in a strategic, coordination or business partnering capacity, for example as a Chief of Staff, Senior Business Partner, Executive Assistant, management consultant or strategy professional.

• 
Strong stakeholder management across complex, matrixed organisations, with the ability to align diverse interests and influence outcomes without formal authority.

• 
A proven ability to influence senior leaders across functions and organizational boundaries, including VP and SVP-level stakeholders.

• 
Demonstrated experience shaping organizational strategy, operating models and leadership agendas in complex global organizations.

• 
A proven ability to structure ambiguity, connect competing priorities and translate strategy into actionable plans.

• 
Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn complex IT, digital and organisational topics into simple, business-relevant messages that land with senior stakeholders.

• 
Strong stakeholder intelligence, with the ability to understand what matters to key partners, anticipate concerns and ensure the right people are involved early enough to create alignment.

• 
Track record of leading strategic transformation initiatives with measurable organizational impact.

• 
Experience with strategic planning, portfolio prioritization, business case development and investment governance.

• 
The confidence to act as a trusted sparring partner to the VP, challenging and strengthening thinking, communication and follow-through before key leadership forums.

• 
A confident approach to using AI to work more effectively and bring modern ways of working.

• 
Resilience, discretion and a calm, senior presence in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English at a professional level.

• 
A master's degree in economics, business administration, finance or a related business discipline.

In addition, it is valued if you have:

• Experience from large, global matrix organisations such as pharmaceuticals, FMCG or consulting.

• Familiarity with IT or Operational Technology (OT) environments.

What you'll do

You will act as the primary strategic coordination and integration point for the GMS IT Vice President and Leadership Team. The role is about ensuring the VP and Leadership Team operate with focus, clarity and influence, so GMS IT is seen as a strategic business partner across GMS and Enterprise IT. You will:

• 
Own the strategic planning process for GMS IT, ensuring priorities, investments, organizational capabilities and operating model decisions are aligned with GMS and Enterprise IT objectives.

• 
Drive continuous improvement of GMS IT leadership effectiveness, governance, decision-making processes and organizational performance.

• 
Help position the GMS IT Vice President and Leadership Team as a strategic partner by shaping clear narratives, framing dilemmas, preparing decision points and translating priorities into executive messages.

• 
Anticipate upcoming leadership moments, stakeholder concerns and business planning needs, ensuring the VP and Leadership Team are prepared, aligned and influential in senior forums.

• 
Represent GMS IT in key cross-functional and enterprise forums, influencing decisions and priorities that impact GMS-wide technology and digital transformation initiatives.

• 
Actively engage key partners across GMS Business Support and Enterprise IT, ensuring they are brought in early and sufficiently involved in business planning and leadership team discussions.

• 
Drive the business planning processes in close collaboration with Finance, People & Organisation and other key functions.

• 
Serve as a member of the GMS IT Leadership Team, driving preparation, follow-up and execution of leadership meetings.

• 
Provide leadership and direction across the GMS IT Business Partner community, creating alignment and consistency in strategic planning, communications and execution across the organization.

• 
Develop stakeholder engagement plans and prepare executive-level communications, leadership updates and strategic storylines that make GMS IT’s contribution visible and easy to understand.

• 
Drive follow-up on key initiatives, ensuring alignment and follow-through across functions and organisational levels.

Who you'll work with

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to bring molecules, processes, devices and products to the people who need them. You will be part of GMS IT, a global organisation spread across the world, working closely with the GMS IT Vice President and Leadership Team.

Your key partners will include Enterprise IT, GMS Business Support, Finance, People & Organisation, the broader Business Partner network and the Enterprise IT Executive Assistant network. You will need to know these partners well, understand how to bring them into the right discussions at the right time, and use that network to create stronger alignment around GMS IT priorities. You will navigate a complex matrix in a virtual setting with cultural awareness and agility, bringing different perspectives together to create clarity and momentum.

What you can expect here

You will join an environment where your expertise shapes decisions at the top of a global organisation. The role offers broad exposure across functions and leadership, the chance to influence how a senior leadership team operates and is perceived, and the opportunity to turn complexity into clear direction. You will be supported to perform at your best while working at pace with curious, ambitious colleagues.

As Associate Director, you will build and lead Microbial Expression Delivery, a newly established department that turns microbial expression technologies into dependable protein and peptide deliveries for Novo’s research portfolio. You will set clear direction for a team of 12 scientists and technicians, sharpen handovers and help research projects move with pace and predictability. Your leadership will get researchers the proteins and data they need sooner, supporting progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine scientific depth in microbial expression with the leadership to bring people together around shared priorities.

• An advanced degree in molecular biology, biotechnology, biochemistry or another relevant scientific discipline.

• People leadership experience and a track record of building trust, developing colleagues and delivering results through collaboration across functions.

• Solid experience with microbial expression of proteins and peptides, and an understanding of how analytical and automated workflows, including LC-MS, turn scientific insight into reliable project impact.

• Experience working in a project-driven or similar matrixed organisation, with the ability to communicate clearly about priorities, dependencies and expectations.

• A collaborative, curious, pragmatic and inclusive way of leading: you invite different perspectives and make it easy for others to succeed through clear direction and respect.

Useful, but not essential:

A PhD in a relevant scientific field.

What you’ll do

You will establish a department that gives colleagues across the Centre for Expression Engineering (CEE) one clear place to request high-quality proteins, peptides and data, and a team that delivers them timely.

• Establish Microbial Expression Delivery as a new department that centralises automated expression technologies and takes end-to-end ownership of timely protein deliveries across the portfolio.

• Take responsibility for our centralised technology platforms, including LC-MS, automated high-throughput workflows, and variant and expression feasibility testing, with clear accountability across interfaces.

• Translate portfolio priorities into clear direction for your team, balancing capacity, dependencies and stakeholder needs to keep deliveries predictable.

• Strengthen handovers and speed up shared deliverables with other CEE departments and internal partners, such as cell line generation, expression optimisation, feasibility assessments, technology implementation and proof-of-concept work.

• Remove organisational barriers across Therapeutic Discovery, apply modular, end-to-end ways of working and align priorities so decisions are made faster.

• Lead visibly: role-model scientific excellence and open communication, and build a respectful, challenge-safe culture where people grow and contribute their best.

Who you’ll work with

You will lead the Microbial Expression Delivery team, made up of 12 scientists and technicians, within the Centre for Expression Engineering. CEE is part of Research Centres of Excellence (RCE), which supports Novo’s research portfolio by enabling microbial strain engineering, strain development and protein production.

Your closest partners are the other CEE departments, scientific and automation experts, and project teams who request deliverables from your centralised workflows. You will also work with colleagues across Therapeutic Discovery, of which RCE is an integral part. In a matrixed organisation, your role is to create clarity on priorities, agree who owns what and keep work moving.

You will work out of our largest research centre in Måløv, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to build something new and given the support to do it well. You will work with scientific and automation experts, shape how a new capability is set up, and grow your leadership alongside a team that values quality, simplicity and impact.

Clear expectations and a culture that rewards results mean you can focus on delivering your best work. You will also help create the same conditions for your team: an open, collaborative and inclusive environment where colleagues can thrive, develop and make their voices heard.

Project Manager – Operations

Location: Lyngby, Denmark

Do you have a proven track record of turning complex operational challenges into tangible results? Are you motivated by getting close to manufacturing operations, analysing performance and working with teams to implement improvements that make a measurable difference?

We are looking for a Project Manager who combines strong analytical and problem-solving capability with the drive, resilience and hands-on approach required to deliver outcomes in complex manufacturing environments.

If you enjoy taking ownership, solving difficult problems and seeing your work translate into improved operational performance, this could be your next career move.

The position

As a Project Manager, you will work as part of our internal operations and manufacturing consulting team, delivering complex improvement, operational readiness and ramp up projects across our global manufacturing network.

This is not a traditional PMO or project coordination role.

You will be expected to get close to the operation, spend time on the shop floor, understand what is really happening within the production environment and use data and structured problem-solving to identify opportunities for improvement.

More importantly, your responsibility does not end when the solution has been identified. You will work alongside manufacturing teams and stakeholders to turn recommendations into actions and deliver tangible operational outcomes.

Our projects are typically intensive assignments, with project teams substantially dedicated to one project at a time. Assignments will often run for six to twelve months and can sometimes continue for longer.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Taking ownership of project workstreams and operational improvement initiatives from diagnosis through to implementation and delivery.

• Driving operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, helping manufacturing operations achieve stable target performance.

• Working directly with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams to understand operational challenges and identify bottlenecks, losses and improvement opportunities.

• Analysing operational performance data and developing capacity models, process maps and improvement scenarios.

• Translating complex analysis into clear recommendations, practical implementation roadmaps and measurable actions.

• Driving implementation and following improvements through to tangible operational outcomes.

• Working with production teams to establish sustainable changes in performance and ways of working.

• Collaborating with stakeholders across manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain and site leadership.

• Influencing stakeholders and maintaining momentum when implementation is challenging or priorities change.

• Communicating progress, risks, recommendations and outcomes clearly to relevant stakeholders and project leadership.

This is a hands on role. You should be comfortable moving between analytical problem-solving and the realities of implementation on the manufacturing shop floor.

The position is based in Lyngby, Denmark, and requires flexibility for up to 50% global travel.

Travel requirements will depend on project assignment and may change throughout a project. The ability and willingness to travel flexibly according to business and project requirements is therefore an essential requirement of the position.

Qualifications

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate a proven track record of delivering outcomes, rather than simply participating in projects.

You combine strong intellectual and analytical capability with the practical judgement, resilience and persistence required to turn ideas into results.

To succeed in this role, you:

• Hold a relevant degree in engineering, science, business administration, economics or another relevant discipline.

• Have relevant professional experience within areas such as manufacturing, operational excellence, operations consulting, engineering, supply chain, procurement or complex cross-functional project work.

• Can demonstrate a proven track record of taking ownership and delivering tangible outcomes through projects, operational improvements or complex cross-functional initiatives.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and structured problem-solving capability.

• Are comfortable personally analysing operational data and using it to identify performance gaps, bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

• Can translate analysis into practical recommendations and then follow those recommendations through implementation.

• Are comfortable working hands-on with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams.

• Can operate effectively in complex and ambiguous environments where the solution may not initially be obvious.

• Demonstrate strong stakeholder management, collaboration and communication skills.

• Have the resilience and persistence to continue driving change when implementation is difficult or initial solutions do not deliver the expected results.

• Are professionally proficient in English.

• Are able and willing to travel globally for up to 50% of your time according to project requirements.

Relevant experience from operations or management consulting can be particularly valuable, including experience gained within operational practices or projects.

We are also interested in candidates from complex manufacturing environments such as pharmaceuticals, automotive, aerospace and FMCG, particularly where you have worked with operational improvement, production ramp-up, manufacturing performance or Lean ways of working.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing, GMP and validation experience are advantageous but are not essential.

Experience working within a Lean manufacturing environment can also be beneficial. Formal Lean certification is not required.

Likewise, formal project management qualifications such as PMP or PRINCE2 are not a requirement. We place greater emphasis on your demonstrated ability to structure problems, work with people, take ownership and deliver measurable outcomes.

About the department

You will join Drug Product Manufacturing Excellence, a global unit responsible for driving performance improvements, operational readiness and transformation across Novo's manufacturing network.

The team operates as an internal operations and manufacturing consultancy, supporting our manufacturing organisation with complex operational challenges.

Our colleagues bring diverse professional backgrounds, including operations and management consulting, Novo manufacturing and support functions, and industries such as automotive, aerospace and FMCG.

What brings the team together is the ability to combine analytical problem-solving with hands-on implementation.

Our projects can include operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, improving capacity and performance within existing operations and solving complex cross-functional manufacturing challenges.

Rather than managing several projects simultaneously, our project teams are typically substantially dedicated to one assignment, allowing them to work closely with the operation and remain involved from diagnosis through to implementation.

As a Project Manager, you will have meaningful ownership within these assignments and will be expected to demonstrate that your work ultimately translates into operational outcomes.

The role provides significant exposure to different manufacturing environments, functions and senior stakeholders across our global organisation and offers opportunities to progress towards increasingly complex project and leadership responsibilities.

Working at Novo

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Associate Consumer Finance & Online Partnerships Director, you will build the financial foundation for how Novo grows online partnerships in Obesity across Europe and Canada (EUCAN). This is a newly created role: you will set up a European customer profit and loss view and a clear business case approach, so teams know where to invest and can track the return. You will turn complex analysis into decisions that help more people reach treatment.

What you’ll bring

You thrive where commercial business development, consumer behaviour and financial decision making meet. You can build something new, influence without formal authority and turn complexity into action.

• A master’s degree in economics, business administration, finance or an equivalent field.

• Significant experience in commercial finance, business development, M&A finance, financial system change projects or customer profitability, including cross-country, regional or global exposure.

• Strong financial modelling and data interpretation skills.

• Practical experience in pricing, negotiation, customer profitability and stakeholder management in a large organisation.

• Experience bringing structure to new business areas, setting clear priorities and steering the business through influence and relationships.

• The ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations and to build new capabilities, standards and frameworks from the ground up.

• Proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, AI modelling, SAP and systematic data consolidation.

• Fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience from consumer health companies, including private healthcare organisations.

• Additional languages.

What you’ll do

You will be the finance partner who helps Region Europe and Canada decide where to invest in online partnerships and consumer initiatives, and who shows what those investments deliver.

• Create the framework and shape commercial partnership priorities through sound financial modelling, working with business partners to assess partnership opportunities and consumer investment initiatives.

• Develop and deliver a business case methodology across European markets, so investment decisions are prudent, comparable and grounded in facts as part of the business rhythm.

• Establish an end-to-end view of customer and partner profit and loss, including system tracking and performance updates that follow return on investment.

• Deliver complex cross-functional change projects with Business Development, Finance, Legal, Supply Chain and Commercial Strategy to enable online sales in new European markets.

• Act as Commercial Finance Partner to the commercial unit for business development and to the UK affiliate.

• Improve data definitions, ownership, quality and comparability of online sales channels across markets.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Business Finance team in Region Europe and Canada (EUCAN), part of International Operations, reporting to the Director of Business Finance. The team is a key business partner to the Regional Leadership Team and the European sales affiliates.

Day to day, you will collaborate with European sales affiliate offices, local finance and business development teams, and with colleagues in Marketing, Business Development and Commercial Excellence, Data, Insights & Analytics, Pricing and Access, and Supply Chain. You will build bridges between these functions, so every investment decision rests on evidence and aims to maximise patient reach. Working across markets, you will help drive both the online sales agenda and the consumer finance agenda in Obesity.

The role is based in Ørestad, Copenhagen, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will shape a new area from the start, with the trust to set direction and the visibility to influence decisions across European markets. Working with colleagues from finance, commercial, legal and supply chain, you will broaden your perspective across the value chain and build new skills through practical, cross-functional experience.

You will be supported to perform at your best, with clear expectations and a culture that values honest input and follows through on decisions.

jobs.occupation: Up to 3 PhD fellowships in Quantum error correction
jobs.description:
The Quantum error correction team at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) invites applicants for up to three PhD fellowships.

  The start date is (expected to be) 1 April, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The programme
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Program (NQCP), funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, is building a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge program in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, the ambition is to build a mission-driven full-stack approach which will involve exciting innovations at every level, from the quantum processor to the quantum-classical interface, all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. The vision of the programme is to enable the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve important problems in the life sciences.

  The project
 Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires low logical error rates together with resource-efficient, experimentally feasible approaches to quantum error correction. Our research spans low-overhead quantum error-correcting codes, efficient syndrome extraction, high-fidelity parity measurements, and scalable hardware architectures. We aim to connect these efforts with fault-tolerant logical operations, taking into account the noise characteristics, connectivity, and operational constraints of quantum computing platforms. In our work, we are collaborating closely with all of the different teams at NQCP; see nqcp.ku.dk.

  We are looking for up to three motivated PhD candidates to undertake research within theoretical effort for quantum error-correction. We are interested in developing a project plan with prospective candidates to best match their skills and experience to the activities in the QEC team. We imagine that the candidates would undertake research within one or more of the following topics:

   	
• Investigation of low-overhead and high-threshold error-correctable codes, including low-density parity check codes 	
• Resource estimation and optimization for scalable quantum computing over different hardware platforms 	
• Distributed quantum error correction on modular design and quantum networks 	
• Optimization of syndrome extraction circuits, error correction cycle, and fault-tolerant logical operation   Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of Physics, Computational Physics, Quantum Information, or a closely related field, with a focus on theoretical and/or computational quantum physics.

  Successful candidates will have:

   	
• Strong analytical and computational skills 	
• Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and quantum information 	
• An interest in developing quantum error correction methods that account for hardware capabilities and limitations 	
• A passion for developing theoretical protocols 	
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic research environment 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction or quantum computing platforms, including photonic systems and superconducting circuits, is an advantage.   Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by the NNF Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.

  The project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Maryam Khanahmadi, maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk, QEC team lead, and the principal supervisor will be Stefano Paesani, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed 
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. a degree in Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Quantum Information or similar. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full-time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Good language and communication skills 	
• Willingness to work in a team 	
• Willingness to engage actively with the other teams at NQCP    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Please note that there is the possibility of including an educational part to the PhD project. Therefore, please indicate in the application whether you would be interested in this.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original degree diplomas and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline
 The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You will be notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Maryam Khanahmadi: maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a 3-year PhD stipend in the field of quantum control theory for quantum algorithms within the general study programme Electronical and Electronic Engineering, as per January 1st 2027, or soon hereafter.

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Your work tasks

The position is part of the research project QUANTA – Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. Real quantum computers are open quantum systems: noise and decoherence act on the computation while it runs, so the idealised picture of a sequence of perfect unitary gates acting on an isolated system does not hold in practice. QUANTA therefore regards a quantum program as an open dynamical system, described by Kraus operators in discrete time and by the controlled Lindblad master equation in continuous time, and treats the choice of quantum gates as control decisions. The aim is to use control theory to design quantum algorithms, in particular optimisation algorithms, that are robust to noise and disturbances.

As a PhD student you will work mainly on two parts of the project. The first concerns reach-avoidance for quantum systems: computing the probability that a quantum process reaches a target set of states before it enters a set of forbidden states, and designing control strategies, for example by dynamic programming, that steer the computation towards its goal while respecting such constraints. You will develop this theory for quantum Markov chains described by Kraus operators and for continuous-time systems described by the Lindblad master equation.

The second part applies these results to quantum optimisation. You will develop algorithms in which an optimisation problem, starting with semidefinite programming and continuing with bilinear and polynomial problems, is solved by a quantum system regarded as a control system, including constrained problems formulated as reach-avoidance. You will analyse how the resulting quantum circuits scale with the problem size and test the algorithms on a real quantum computer.

You will work closely with the principal investigator, a postdoctoral researcher on the project and the project's international collaborators, and the project includes research stays at partner institutions abroad. You will present your results at international conferences and in scientific journals, and they will form the basis of your PhD thesis. As part of the PhD programme you will follow PhD courses and take part in teaching and supervision of student projects at the department.

Your competencies You hold a Master's degree in control engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with a solid mathematical background, for example in linear algebra, dynamical systems, control theory, optimisation or probability theory, and with a genuine interest in quantum computing.

Knowledge of quantum mechanics or quantum information is an advantage, but not a requirement – what matters is that you are motivated to learn it during the project. Programming experience, for example in Python, is also an advantage. We value curiosity, the ability to work independently and the willingness to share ideas and help colleagues. You communicate well in English, both orally and in writing.

Qualification requirements

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

The position is hosted by the Learning and Decisions Lab at the Department of Electronic Systems, Aalborg University, led by Professor Rafal Wisniewski. The lab develops theory and algorithms at the intersection of control theory, stochastic systems, optimisation and quantum computing, including stability and safety of stochastic and quantum systems and feedback control of quantum hardware. You will join a team of senior researchers, PhD students and postdoctoral fellows working on related problems, in an informal and international environment with weekly meetings and close day-to-day supervision

Salary and terms of employment
